subject: MercuryMart: Checkout errors & p99 spikes after v4.2 quant flip — immediate rollback?
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@mercurymart.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@mercurymart.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Checkout failures and p99 spikes since v4.2 quant flip

Jonas —

We pushed the v4.2 model + new quantization profile last night (per your rollout notes). Since ~02:00 PT this morning we've seen:
- Checkout throughput drop ~28%
- P99 latency jump from 420ms -> 1.8s on cart-affecting calls
- Intermittent 500s during high concurrency (approx 0.6% of requests)

Attached are a sample error_dump_0617.log and a short trace. Our SRE has correlation to the model-serving pool (requests entering qprofile-enabled nodes). This is blocking checkout for some customers. Samir and I are available for an emergency call — please advise immediate mitigation (rollback?) and an ETA to stabilize.

We need clear next steps and a targeted timeline — finance and ops are asking for an exec summary.

Thanks,
Claire
Director, Platform Engineering — MercuryMart
[attachment: error_dump_0617.log (text/plain)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@mercurymart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures and p99 spikes since v4.2 quant flip

Claire — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. Marking this P0.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- I've pinged eng (Irene + Dylan) to triage and confirm whether the new quant kernel is causing degrade.
- If a hot rollback is safest, we will propose a 2-hour maintenance window and coordinate with your ops so user-facing traffic is protected.
- Internal exec loop: copying Marissa (CS) for customer comms; will loop in Aditya (sales leadership) if we need credits/contract-level remediation.

Can you confirm whether MercuryMart needs us to schedule the rollback in a specific maintenance window (overnight local) or do you want immediate rollback now? Also please share SRE traces for the 500s if available.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Sent from mobile]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Checkout failures and p99 spikes since v4.2 quant flip

Jonas / team — initial triage below (summary):
- Observed behavior: long-context decode paths (cart + rec end-to-end) hit a quantized attention kernel path that falls back to an emulated float path when a cache miss occurs. That fallback is significantly slower for sequences >512 tokens and under concurrency it induces retries in our runtime.
- Error pattern: the 500s appear to be an upstream timeout triggered when the request exceeds our internal retry budget (we're seeing ~3-4 retries on some requests).
- Repro: We reproduced locally with MercuryMart sample payload (attached trace_snapshot_0617.json).

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Immediate rollback to v4.1 + previous qprofile (fastest, will restore p99 & throughput; requires brief 2h maintenance)
2) Apply a runtime patch to disable the fallback kernel path for quantized instances (medium effort, risk of surface regressions, ~6-12h work)
3) Traffic route: divert MercuryMart traffic to non-qprofile pool (works quickly if capacity exists in non-quant pool)

Recommendation: rollback to v4.1 now (option 1) while we investigate root cause and build a non-fallback quanta path. I will open RED-9142 for postmortem and a patch PR.

Irene Choi
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
[attachment: trace_snapshot_0617.json (application/json)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@mercurymart.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Checkout failures and p99 spikes since v4.2 quant flip

Claire —
Thanks for raising this and for the logs. Per Irene's analysis, rolling back to v4.1 is the least-risk immediate mitigation.

Proposal for next steps (we'll move as soon as we have your sign-off):
- Rollback window: Thu 17 Jun 2027, 11:30 PM - 01:30 AM PT (2 hours) — will execute a canary rollback, monitor p50/p95/p99 and error-rate, and abort if any regression observed.
- Customer comms: we'll send a status update at start, at 30m, & at completion.
- Post-incident: Eng to provide RCA and a timeline for a non-fallback quant kernel.

If you prefer immediate rollback now, we can do that but it will impact users during our daytime — please confirm which you prefer.

Separately, I'm looping in Aditya for commercial remediation (credits / SLA).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Commercial remediation: offer MercuryMart a 10% credit on June invoices given the production impact (pending CS confirmation). Marissa, please prepare the credit note and exec summary for Claire's leadership.

Aditya Rao
